verses.1: And the word of Jehovah was to me:
verses.2: The son of Adam faced a difficult situation, and he went to the house of Israel.
verses.3: And you said, “Thus it is said: ‘O Adonai Yehovah, the great one! Your wings are wide; your wings are long. Your body is filled with strength. The wound that was inflicted upon him came to Laban. And he took the rope of the tree.’”
verses.4: He took the head of his son and brought it to the land of Canaan, in the city of Rekhelim Shamo.
verses.5: And he took some seeds from the earth and placed them in a field. He chose seeds that could grow in large quantities.
verses.6: And it grew into a tree that was humble and lowly. Its branches reached towards him, and its roots were beneath him. It became a tree that shed fruit.
verses.7: And there was a great bird with wings as wide as wings of a bird. Its body was covered with feathers. And behold, that flower was placed on its back, and its legs were used to hold it up so that it could be watered from the watering pots in the garden.
verses.8: To a good field, to many waters – that is what it means to grow branches and bear fruit, so that it can become an adarot vine.
verses.9: Say, “Thus said Adonai Jehovah: May its roots be destroyed, and may its fruits be plundered. All the branches of its tree will be cut down; no large branches or many people will be able to pick them up from their roots.”
verses.10: And behold, the flower that was planted did not succeed; instead, the spirit of death took hold of it. It withered away on its own.
verses.11: And the word of Jehovah came to me, saying:
verses.12: Say to the house of Meribah, “Do you not know what these people are? Look, the king of Babylon has come to Jerusalem. He took away the queen and her officials, and brought them before him in Babylon.”
verses.13: And he took a female lamb from the flock of the king, and made a covenant with it. Then he brought it back to him along with the sheep of the land.
verses.14: To be a humble queen, one must not dare to break her covenant with God.
verses.15: And he rebelled against sending his slaves out of Egypt. He wanted to have horses and a large army. But he failed in his attempts. He broke the covenant he had made, and was punished accordingly.
verses.16: O Lord, I beg you, do not let it happen in the place where the king who rules over him resides. He has broken his covenant with him during the time of Babylon’s destruction.
verses.17: And it will not be done by a large army or by a large crowd of people. Pharaoh will do it in battle, by slaying many people and destroying their lives.
verses.18: And in this way, he broke the covenant. And behold, he gave his hand, and all these things were done without any resistance.
verses.19: Therefore, thus said Adonai Yehovah: “I will live if not my angel, who is here. And I will fulfill the covenant I made with him.”
verses.20: And I spread a covering over him; he was captured in my hands. They brought him before me, and I judged him there, above the throne.
verses.21: And all their fugitives in every direction will fall. Those who remain will be scattered to every wind. And know that I, the LORD, have spoken.
verses.22: Thus said Adonai YHWH: “I will take it from the heights of Mount Sinai. I will take it from its summit, and I will place it on the high mountain.”
verses.23: In Mount Merom, Israel, we planted it. It grew branches and produced fruit. It became a great tree. We settled under its branches, with all the birds resting there. Every wing of the bird rested on its branches.
verses.24: And all the trees in the forest shall know that I, the LORD, have humbled those tall trees. I’ve made lowly trees stand tall, and I’ve made barren trees bear fruit. I, the LORD, have spoken and done these things.
